strings.name: Anthony Capuano
strings.role: President and Chief Executive Officer of Marriott International
strings.summary: Anthony Capuano is president and CEO of Marriott International. He joined the company in 1995 and spent many years overseeing hotel development, design and operations services. He became CEO in 2021 and added the presidency in 2023, with responsibilities spanning owner relationships, brand expansion and corporate operations.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026, with the November 2 quarterly release as recent evidence. His birth year remains unconfirmed. Appointment dates are distinguished from announcements; not every hotel carrying a group brand is company-owned.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributes to Marriott hotel development and corporate management, advancing its global hotel network, brands and lodging services.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: A member of Cornell University's class of 1987, he earned a bachelor's degree in hotel administration.
strings.facts.f2.label: Business model
strings.facts.f2.value: Marriott operates lodging brands through franchising, management and licensing, among other arrangements. The size of its brand network is not its count of owned hotels.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Global hotel development
strings.highlights.h1.text: Starting in market planning and feasibility, he progressed to global development, design and operations responsibilities, balancing the needs of owners, developers and operators.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Operations during the pandemic
strings.highlights.h2.text: The appointment announcement credits him with leading work on Commitment to Clean. This concerned operating standards, not demonstrated health outcomes.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Comments on third-quarter results
strings.timeline.t1.text: The company release includes his operating assessment. Reported quarterly net income was $794 million; the full-year outlook remained a forecast.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Selected for Cornell hospitality honor
strings.timeline.t2.text: Cornell announces his selection as its 2026 Hospitality Icon of the Industry. This announcement alone does not establish attendance at an award ceremony.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Adds Marriott presidency
strings.timeline.t3.text: The board decided on February 10 to add the presidency, effective February 24. He was already CEO and a director.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Appointed CEO and director
strings.timeline.t4.text: The SEC filing records the appointment as effective that day. The company issued its release on February 23; the dates should not be conflated.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes group president
strings.timeline.t5.text: He becomes group president of global development, design and operations services, a role distinct from his later presidency of Marriott International.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Takes global development responsibility
strings.timeline.t6.text: He becomes executive vice president and global chief development officer, adding oversight of global design in 2014.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Marriott
strings.timeline.t7.text: He joins the market planning and feasibility team, assessing new and existing hotel projects.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduates from Cornell
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earns a bachelor's degree in hotel administration and later maintains alumni and advisory board ties to the school.
